Notes

Face means expression, dignity and pose. Jackzebra cooks social language into gruesome jokes, then YoungQueenz answers with an inventory of possessions, feeling and momentum.

挂起个脸

挂脸 or 挂着脸 describes visibly wearing a displeased, stern, or unfriendly expression. It is an outward social signal, rather than necessarily an emotionless “poker face.” The proverb about dignity later lets 脸 move from a visible expression to the standing a person protects.

  • Lyric text
撑起一片天

撑起一片天 pictures supporting a whole space above oneself. As a figurative phrase, it suggests taking responsibility or establishing a place where one can stand independently. Beside earning little but refusing deception, the boast concerns sustaining a life on one’s own terms.

  • Lyric text
知识

The expected payoff of acquiring knowledge would be competence or income. Here it is followed by a refusal to deceive, even if that means earning little. The verse establishes an ethical limit before it begins flaunting artistic lawlessness: refusing a scam and refusing restraint are presented as compatible forms of self-respect.

  • Lyric transcript
树要层皮人要张脸

This is a variant of the proverb that people have faces as trees have bark: a person needs dignity and a sense of shame. Following the refusal to deceive for money, it makes 'face' a matter of self-respect. The title can therefore resonate with both facial expression and social standing.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 人有臉樹有皮
  • Chinese lyric transcript
当导演

The wish to direct a film is immediately realized in words: people enter a pot, the rules belong to the speaker, and so does the script. The grotesque scene reads as a declaration of artistic control. “This is art” then works as its punchline—the director claims the authority to call even his ugliest invention art.

  • Lyric transcript
自来熟

自来熟 describes someone who becomes familiar with strangers immediately. The pivot is 熟, shú, which means both 'familiar' and 'cooked.' Put people in a boiling pot and they will get 'familiar' without a social app: the line makes a social idiom literal as a gruesome joke.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 熟
  • Wiktionary: 自來熟
  • Chinese lyric transcript
度

度, dù, can mean a degree, a measure, or a proper limit. Here jokes have no 度; a few lines later 温度, wēndù, explicitly names temperature, inside a sequence about boiling and heat. The same character links social restraint to the physically excessive cooking joke.

  • Lyric text
规则是我定的

In “Discipline,” rules organize frightened people beneath somebody else’s hand. Here the first person claims authorship of rules and content together. The repetition of 我, “I,” makes control audible, but its setting inside an absurd cooking scene keeps the boast theatrical: this is the miniature world the rapper can make in a verse.

  • Lyric transcript
不怕开水烫的死猪

死猪不怕开水烫 says that a dead pig no longer fears being scalded. It describes someone beyond intimidation, often because they have lost any shame. Following the earlier insistence that people need dignity, the proverb introduces its unruly opposite. The face must be protected, yet artistic bravado also claims the freedom of someone with nothing left to lose.

  • Hanzi dictionary: 死猪不怕開水燙
  • Chinese lyric transcript
戴着帽子低着头

The face that began the song becomes hard to see. 帽子, head lowered, and uninterrupted walking give aloofness a physical routine. The next repeated joke about looking cool exposes that routine as a recognizable pose, so the image both protects the speaker from others and offers them something to admire.

  • Lyric transcript
装逼

装逼 means putting on airs or performing impressiveness, with a coarse, mocking edge. “So cool” praises the very thing 装逼 discredits, leaving the pose both ridiculous and attractive. The preceding hat-down walk is a ready-made image of aloofness. The refrain lets us enjoy that image while noticing how hard it works to look effortless.

  • Lyric text
commes

“Commes” and “ricks” are fashion shorthand for Comme des Garçons and Rick Owens. They enter the verse without explanation, like items an initiated listener is expected to recognize. The repeated “I got” makes labels, people, love and pain grammatically equivalent possessions; the inventory grows beyond clothes without changing its structure.

  • COMME des GARÇONS: official stores
  • Rick Owens: official collections
  • Lyric text
young ozma

OZMA is a name YoungQueenz uses on his own Bandcamp and SoundCloud profiles. The paired “young zeebra / young ozma” places the two collaborators inside the same rolling list. It also shifts from ordinary possessions to identities: the verse can announce who they are with the same economy it uses to name what they have.

  • YoungQueenz: official Bandcamp profile
  • YoungQueenz / OZMA: official SoundCloud profile
  • Chinese lyric transcript
i got pain

Pain receives exactly the same “I got” construction as clothes, girls and love. That repetition prevents the boast from becoming a clean account of prosperity. The verse can accumulate everything wanted and still accumulate hurt; its quick refusal of enemies is the first item it decisively excludes from the collection.

  • Lyric transcript
堅持比放棄容易

The expected motivational comparison makes perseverance harder and quitting easier. YoungQueenz reverses it: continuing is now the easier action. Beside the catalog of things he has and places he tours, the reversal sounds like momentum or commitment becoming habitual.

  • Lyric text

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
